Login sequence (Telnet, port 23/2324 via NAT):

Welcome to EPON.


User Access Verification

Username: admin
Password: admin

Epon>

Unprivileged prompt is "Epon> ". "help" is NOT a valid command ("% Unknown command: help") -- the discovery command is "?".

Epon>?
  enable  Turn on privileged mode command
  exit    Exit current mode and down to previous mode
  list    Print command list
  ping    ping functions
  show    Show running system information

NOTE ON SYNTAX ORDER: the "list" command (full grammar reference, see below)
places the optional vendor-keyword in parentheses FIRST and the INTERFACE
placeholder in the position it actually occupies on the command line -- do
not assume INTERFACE always comes last. Examples actually verified working
on this unit:
  show epon sfp-info 1/1          (keyword "sfp-info" BEFORE the interface)
  show epon 1/1 optical-ddm       (interface BEFORE the keyword "optical-ddm")
  show onu optical-ddm epon 1/1 1 (onu optical-ddm epon <IF> <onu-id>)
  show onu config epon 1/1 1      (onu config epon <IF> <onu-id>)
  show pon 1 statistic            (bare port number, no "epon" keyword, no slash)
  show nni 1 statistic            (bare port number, same pattern)
A command guessed by "probably symmetric" ordering was tried and rejected
by the device ("show epon 1/1 sfp-info" -> "% Unknown command"). Always
verify the exact token order against the "list" output or a live "?"
before using a new show/config command in the driver.

Epon(config)#interface epon 1/1
Epon(config-epon1/1)#

NOTE: entering this per-EPON-port config context (interface epon <X/Y>) does
NOT by itself change the running-config -- it only moves the CLI prompt one
level deeper, exactly like Cisco IOS "interface" sub-mode. No write/commit
happens until a config-changing command is actually typed inside it.

--- ONU authorization grammar (this is the mechanism that gates
    discoverUnconfiguredOnus / authorizeOnu / blockOnu / unblockOnu) ---

Epon(config-epon1/1)#auth mode ?
  disable  -- Disable auth function
  hybrid   -- Hybrid auth mode
  loid     -- Loid based auth mode
  mac      -- Mac based auth mode

Epon(config-epon1/1)#whitelist ?
  add     -- Add whitelist entry
  clear   -- Clear whitelist table
  delete  -- Delete whitelist entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#whitelist add ?
  MACADDR  -- Mac address.example: 78:5c:72:00:11:22

Epon(config-epon1/1)#blacklist ?
  add     -- Add blacklist entry
  clear   -- Clear blacklist table
  delete  -- Delete blacklist entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#loidlist ?
  add     -- Add loid entry
  clear   -- Clear loid table
  delete  -- Delete loid entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#loidlist add ?
  LOID  -- Loid value, 6-24 character

Epon(config-epon1/1)#add ?
  onu  -- Onu config

Epon(config-epon1/1)#add onu ?
  <1-128>  -- Specified Onu Id

UNVERIFIED: whether "add onu <id>" takes any further argument (e.g. a MAC to
bind to that slot) after the id, or is a complete command as-is. The device
only ever showed "<1-128> -- Specified Onu Id" as the sole completion at
this depth; the next token was never probed because doing so would be the
first state-changing command on this port (no physical ONU exists yet to
safely validate against). DO NOT implement authorizeOnu's "add onu" step
without probing "add onu 1 ?" first, ideally once a real ONU is physically
present so the end-to-end effect can be observed.

  port  -- Config port

CONFIRMED real syntax in actual use on this unit (captured verbatim from
"show running-config", not guessed):
  onu 1 vlan port 1 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 2 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 3 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 4 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
(one line per physical LAN port on the ONU, port numbers 1-4 observed)

--- quirks that any driver/parser MUST account for ---

1. PAGER: some "show" outputs longer than one screen stop with the literal
   line "--- Enter Key To Continue ----" and wait for an Enter keypress
   before continuing (see show_onu_config_paginated.txt). A driver's telnet
   client must detect this marker and send a bare newline to page through,
   or it will hang forever waiting for the real prompt.

2. STREAMING/BLOCKING COMMAND -- AVOID: "show epon <IF> counter-change"
   never returned to the "Epon# " prompt during reconnaissance and appears
   to be a live/continuously-refreshing view (like a "watch"), not a
   one-shot report. Sending it from an automated session with no way to
   send Ctrl+C left the whole telnet session stuck (every subsequent
   command sent in that same session was silently swallowed, interpreted
   as keystrokes inside the live view instead of as new CLI commands).
   Do not use this command in the driver without first confirming the
   correct way to exit it (Ctrl+C was not tested).

3. INTERFACE NAMING IS NOT CONSISTENT ACROSS CONTEXTS for the same physical
   EPON port 1 on slot 1:
     - "show interfaces status"      -> "Epon 1/1"   (capitalized, space)
     - "show vlan" (port membership) -> "Pon1/1"     (no space, "Pon" not "Epon")
     - CLI command argument syntax   -> "epon 1/1"   (lowercase keyword + space + slot/port)
     - "show interfaces brief"       -> does not list EPON ports at all,
       only the GE1/1-4 copper uplinks.
   A driver's parser must not assume one canonical interface-name string
   works across all show commands; each command's own format must be
   parsed on its own terms.

4. "show olt mac" / "show olt mac epon 1/1" only ever showed the table
   header ("ID    mac               valid static_flag aging port_id") with
   zero data rows, because no ONU is physically connected yet. The actual
   column data format for a populated row is UNVERIFIED -- do not write a
   row-parsing regex until a real populated table has been captured.

5. OLT-side optical DDM ("show epon <IF> optical-ddm") only exposes
   Temperature / Voltage / TxBias / TxPower -- there is no RxPower field on
   the OLT's own EPON port, unlike a GPON OLT. This is architecturally
   expected: EPON upstream reception is burst-mode per-ONU, so a
   continuous "RxPower" reading for the whole PON port does not apply the
   same way it would on a GPON card. Per-ONU optical data (if/when it
   becomes available) must come from "show onu optical-ddm epon <IF> <id>"
   once an ONU is actually online -- today it only yields
   "! Onu <id> is offline!".

6. "show version" / "show system" never required paging (one screen).
   "show running-config" / "show interfaces status" were multi-section
   but also fit without triggering the pager on this unit's current
   (nearly-empty) configuration; a production config with many VLANs/ONUs
   provisioned may trigger the pager on these too.
